The bug will be fixed in the next release.

Cheers,
Yang

messages.subject: Re: SAM_pairer_get_next_read_BIN: Assertion `l_name < 256' failed.
messages.body_plain:
I've also been playing around with the source code some more to try to figure out what's going on here.

The process appears to be parsing the original bam file, which is name-sorted, and finds that there are some multi-mapping reads. In this original file, it's parsing the header just fine. It then creates a new bam file:

    temp-core-023711-D067E5FD27D0.sam.fixbam

and when it then reads the header of this file, it gets thrown off somehow about 1/3 of the way through.

Note, the header seems to be fine in this file in that at least 'samtools view -H ' will show the full header with no problem.

When featureCounts is parsing the header in binary format, it's parsing
   a. length of read name
   b. the name of the read itself (based on the length info above)
   c.  the length of that reference sequence.

when it crashes, it seems to have jumped around in the file (my guess) because instead of reading in the length of the next read name, it's actually in the name of some different target.

Some of the things that might make my data set 'special' is that it has ~300k  target sequences in it, so the header is pretty long (as compared to mapping to a reference genome, where you might have tens to hundreds of targets).

I hope this helps!  Please let me know if there's anything else I can do assist here.   The data aren't mine, so I'm checking with the owner to see if I can share it with you.  In case I can, do you have a private way for me to get it to you?  If you give me your direct email address, I can send you a private link to it.

many thanks,

~brian

messages.subject: Re: SAM_pairer_get_next_read_BIN: Assertion `l_name < 256' failed.
messages.body_plain:
The problem is related to the length of our header. Our bam header lists all 300k 'gene' targets, and only a portion of the header ends up getting stored in the buffer that is ultimately parsed by featureCounts. Once the end of

>     thread_context->input_buff_BIN_used

is reached in the #defined function:

> BAM_next_nch

it ends up crashing.

The allocation to this buffer appears to be based on another variable that at some point determines the amount of memory to allocate per thread. Without spending a lot more time on this, I was able to hack the code here in 'input-files.c':

> int SAM_pairer_create(SAM_pairer_context_t * pairer, int all_threads, int bin_buff_size_per_thread, int BAM_input, int is_Tiny_Mode, int is_single_end_m\
>
> ode, int force_do_not_sort, int display_progress, char * in_file, void (* reset_output_function) (void * pairer), int (* output_header_function) (void *\
>
> pairer, int thread_no, int is_text, unsigned int items, char * bin, unsigned int bin_len), int (* output_function) (void * pairer, int thread_no, char \
>
> * bin1, char * bin2), char * tmp_path, void * appendix1, int long_read_minimum_length) {
>
> bin_buff_size_per_thread = 256; // hack bhaas
>
> memset(pairer, 0, sizeof(SAM_pairer_context_t));

and then it appears to work ok.

Is this something you'll be able to address in the next release?

thx in advance,

~brian

messages.subject: Re: SAM_pairer_get_next_read_BIN: Assertion `l_name < 256' failed.
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Brain!

I've found the problem: the BAM file has a relatively lager header. This shouldn't be a problem for featureCounts since it allocates memory according to the BAM header size. However, when the BAM file was from STAR or Picard, featureCounts has to fix its format by creating a temporary BAM file ("fixbam") and copies all the alignment records into this temporary file. The temporary file is not compressed, namely its header is much larger than the header in the original BAM file, but featureCounts still used the original header size to allocate memory. This made featureCounts run out of buffer. Increasing the buffer size as you did can fix this problem with no side effect. Still, this problem will be fixed in the next release.

Cheers,
Yang
